summary.text: A 70-year-old woman was previously admitted to another hospital with an injury from a fall onto bicycle handlebars. Enhanced CT revealed injury in the pancreatic body, and she was transferred to the authors’ hospital 3 h after injury, hemodynamically stable since admission. A previous CT and MRCP did not identify major pancreatic duct disruption.

On the following day, repeat CT showed increased fluid, and amylase was 1100 U/L and lipase 1969 U/L, described as elevated. ERP showed contrast leakage from the injured duct and the pancreatic tail was not visualized. The guidewire crossed the break but the ENPD catheter did not advance; EPS is reported to have failed, and a 5-French ENPD catheter was placed at the injury site preoperatively.

Laparotomy began 22 h after injury and 2 h after ERP and found bloody ascitic fluid, saponification and a partial thickness laceration of the pancreatic body with the ENPD catheter tip at the injury site. She was diagnosed with grade III pancreatic body injury with MPD disruption. The catheter was moved into the distal MPD segment and the duct and laceration were sutured, with 525 mL blood loss and no transfusion required, and pancreatic resection was prevented; the authors state that the pancreas and spleen were preserved.

The postoperative course was uneventful. ERP on POD 31 showed no leakage of contrast medium from the MPD, and the ENPD catheter was changed to an EPS catheter. She was ambulatory and discharged on POD 56, with the EPS catheter planned for 6 months.
